description: A richly appointed private library or study imbued with deep Edwardian or Victorian scholarly character. The walls are lined floor to ceiling with dark walnut bookshelves densely packed with antique leather-bound volumes in warm brown, burgundy, and gold spines. A tall multi-pane window with dark stained wood casing lets in filtered warm daylight from the left, its panes casting warm rectangles of light across the room. In the background, a large richly colored tapestry or embroidered textile — featuring deep crimson, gold, and sage patterns — hangs on the back wall between the shelves, adding an opulent textural element. The focal point is a large round drum table in dark polished mahogany positioned at center frame. On its surface rest an open leather-bound book, a pair of reading glasses, a small ceramic inkwell, a peacock feather, and a small jade or stone decorative object. A warm amber glow pools softly from the table surface, emanating from an ornate object with a forest-green fabric body hung with silk fringe tassels, its warm light washing gently across the open book and table surface below. The palette is deeply saturated: forest green, walnut brown, crimson, and amber gold. The mood is intensely scholarly, romantic, and theatrical — a private sanctuary of accumulated knowledge.
